title: The polynomial ring over a field localized at the origin is regular local of dimension d
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $d\ge0$, $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ the polynomial ring and $\mathfrak p=(x_1,\dots,x_d)\subset R$. Then $\mathfrak p$ is a maximal ideal with $R/\mathfrak p\cong k$, and the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$ whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is generated by the images of $x_1,\dots,x_d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660): for a maximal ideal m of k[x_1..x_n], m is generated by n elements and dim k[x_1..x_n]_m = n, hence k[x_1..x_n]_m is regular local of dimension n; here m = (x_1..x_d)
